What does “gas” mean in crypto? 

“Gas” is important in the world of crypto. Simply put, gas is the payment needed when making a transaction or interacting with a smart contract on a blockchain — i.e., the network fee you pay. 

Gas is usually paid in the given blockchain’s native cryptocurrency — e.g., ETH is used for transactions on Ethereum, and BNB is used for the same on BNB Smart Chain). These fees go to miners or validators responsible for keeping networks secure and confirming transactions. Gas fees also prevent spam on the network, keeping the blockchain running smoothly.

Moraine Lake, Canada 🇨🇦💙✨

Hidden deep within the Valley of the Ten Peaks, Moraine Lake is one of the most breathtaking and dreamlike destinations in the Canadian Rockies. Its waters shimmer in an almost unreal turquoise — a hue so intense, it looks like it was imagined, not found.

Surrounded by colossal peaks, ancient glaciers, and thick evergreen forests, the lake transforms with the light: still and mirror-like at dawn, dazzling under the midday sun, and set ablaze in golden alpenglow at dusk.

Located in Banff National Park, the lake sits just a 20–30 minute drive from Lake Louise. During summer months, access is restricted — most travelers opt for shuttles or guided tours to experience this natural wonder.

Mendenhall Ice Caves, Alaska

Step into the Mendenhall Ice Caves of southeast Alaska, where the entire water cycle unfolds before your eyes in one extraordinary setting. Nestled beneath a 12-mile-long glacier—just a short 12-mile journey from downtown Juneau—these ethereal formations are as rare as they are mesmerizing.

Known originally as Sitaantaagu and Aak’wtaaksit, the glacier gives rise to surreal blue ice caves. Reaching them is an adventure: paddle by kayak to the glacier’s edge, then climb across its rippling surface to discover what lies beneath.

Yet this wonder is vanishing. Driven by climate change, the Mendenhall Glacier has retreated nearly two miles since 1958—and continues to shrink each year.

The caves themselves emerge from meltwater carving through ancient ice, creating dreamlike, transient chambers often described as otherworldly. Their beauty is undeniable—but so is their fragility.
